correctness.rationale: Read Chen’s five preconditional axioms P1–P5 and three F-algebra laws directly in Definition 3.1/3.3; confirmed Holliday antitone-negation Proposition 1. On Boolean P(V), N(∅)=V, N antitone, A∩N(A)=∅ and A⊆N(N(A)) imply self-adjoint polarity X⊆N(Y) iff Y⊆N(X); singleton adjacency is symmetric and irreflexive, and singleton tests determine N(A) as the common-neighbor operation of a unique simple graph. Conversely N_G reverses unions to intersections and has semicomplementation and double inflation. Carefully reconstructed P1–P5 for A⇒_G B=N_G(A\B)∪(A∩B), using X=(A∩B)\C for P5; checked conditional identity, normality, modus ponens, induced N_G and negation import only on complete graphs via two nonadjacent vertices. Independently enumerated all 1,2,3,4-vertex simple graphs, checked all subset triples and all laws: 266376 graph-triples, matching the original verified code; this is finite corroboration, while the polarity and conditional identity proofs apply to every n>=1. The count 2^{n choose 2} is explicitly of distinct unary reducts, not binary conditional extensions.

originality.rationale: The correspondence between fundamental negations and symmetric irreflexive graph polarities is standard in substance, and not presented as novel alone. Chen’s 2026 primary full text defines F and describes fundamental lattices; Holliday’s full Preconditionals Proposition 2 lifts any antitone precomplementation as ¬A∨(A∩B), but this generally fails conditional identity for noncomplete G. The reviewed explicit same-carrier Boolean extension with N(A\B), its MP/normality laws and graph-exact negation-import boundary is a substantive stronger result not stated in either source. The earlier fixed-point normal form for finite chains is a different carrier class, and general frame representations need not give identical Boolean carrier.
residual_risks: An earlier unindexed same-carrier lifting theorem for fundamental lattices with distributive/Boolean meet could subsume the formula.

value.rationale: An exact labeled reduct spectrum on a canonical finite Boolean lattice is a natural algebraic classification, and the explicit same-carrier lift resolves a genuine extension issue left by the usual Sasaki-type construction, rather than a trivial relabeling. The coexistence of MP and normality with many nonclassical graph negations, plus sharp complete-graph boundary for negation import, clarifies logical independence and is useful beyond the raw counting formula. No unsupported claim about all binary F-preconditionals or arbitrary lattices.

limitations: Finite nonempty labelled V, Boolean lattice P(V), Chen P1–P5 plus ID, semicomplementation and inflation; no conclusion for arbitrary bounded lattices.
Negation import iff complete is established only for explicitly constructed conditional, not all possible lifts.
